title: The struggle of the repentant against the accuser
english: Having been tested and having experienced the despair of salvation, I myself am being subjected to such thoughts, being deaf and unable to hear, not wishing to refute them, lest by being found guilty of this, I should lose the brief readiness for repentance. For, O Lord, not hoping, I do not dare to assume I will be heard. For, being unable to defend myself, I endure the defense, knowing: 'Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for the wrath, for it is written, Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord' (Ps 37:8).

I am ready and well-disposed toward the lashes of the senses. Indeed, even my pain, through which I suffer for past deeds, is before me, wounding and scourging me. And it can be so; since my pain is such that, while I suffer for the evils I have done, it is necessary to receive lashes besides the sins, I am ready for these, that is, I am ready to be struck for the sake of returning.

The clear sympathy toward us is the memory of the one's own suffering throughout. For, as Paul says, since he himself has suffered, he is able to help those being tempted. Just as according to the law, he who commits sin was mindful of those being offered as a sacrifice for it, so it is to care for one's own sin, hurrying to make the work of repentance right.

While I care for my own sin, those who hate me because I have repented live according to the bad life, being strong and powerful to make me weak according to this life. If even they cast me off as a dead thing to be loathed, but You cover me under Your mighty hand; for when You are present, the enemies are weak and feeble.

Since I am surrounded by enemies, both evil men and invisible powers, I need help; I do not require help from another, but from You, Lord; for You also are found to be the God of my salvation, and the cause of this salvation is God.
King David, having brought the ark of God into Jerusalem, arranged certain men as singers for its liturgy and order, so that the hymns of God might be [heard].

Regarding these, even Jeduthun, as in the list and numbering of the previously mentioned songs in the Chronicles, carries something like this. He who composed the present psalm himself on behalf of David, or having received it from David, proclaimed it. And in the present psalm, the one proclaiming is introduced from repentance into virtue.

Since almost every beginning of sin occurs through speech, he intending to guard his ways through actions sets covenants with himself, so that he might not sin with the tongue. For if the sinless state regarding speech is kept by him, the cleansing from sins according to action will follow; 'For by your words you shall be justified,' he says, 'and by your words you shall be condemned' (Ps 38:2ab); and 'Amen I say to you: regarding every idle word you shall give an account on the day of judgment' (Ps 38:2c).

After the verse, the sinner and there the devil and the evil angel present with the man are called. If anyone, intending to guard his ways for himself so as not to sin in tongue, sets a guard for his mouth, the sinner, representing himself as such in opposition to the one repenting, reminds him of former things, bringing them into the midst as a reproach, wishing to mock through the reminder, so as to drag back into the former sin the one who has turned away from it.

Not so, he says, the one standing as a sinner before me, I was struck dumb toward the words from which I began to speak good things; for having begun not to speak concerning sinlessness, having understood from good doctrines what one must not answer toward provoking words, I was silent, having said nothing to them, so as, the one saying the aforementioned things, not the pain, but having been freed from sins through sense, being renewed and made new, having been pained again by those whom he reproached, saying the things done to me (Ps 38:4ab).

From the words of the one standing as a sinner before me, my heart was heated, being consumed by fire. But since I said nothing from such thoughts within me, the heating was guarded, and 'In my meditation fire shall be burned' (Ps 38:4c). title: Participation in the Image and Divine Discipline
english: With the verse set before him, the fire of such study consumes the pre-existing exhaustion.

Regarding the sinner he says: 'I was deaf and humbled and was silent' (Ps 38:4c); but regarding God: 'I spoke in my tongue' (Ps 38:4c). He who brings forth words in his own tongue from genuine desire and intention is different from him who speaks deceitfully in a foreign tongue. And since we have a tongue even within the human being, which is strictly our own tongue, by which it is possible to speak from a disposition.

Since I have begun to live according to human life and expect its end, this is not clear to me; make known to me my end, so that having learned the multitude of the years of life in the flesh, I may know whom I must aim for (Ps 38:5). What have I accomplished, and what is lacking to me for the completion of perfection? And so it is: since every wise man acts and works toward a certain perfection and goal, it is necessary to have knowledge of this, to know what the end is set for living and what is the number of the days according to the decrees of truth. For one is not wise if he does not know what he lacks for the fulfillment of the goal; just as one intending to take up a certain science asks the teacher: 'Show me how many the decrees of the science are, so that I may know which they are, and by which I lack the peak.'

Having passed from life into the struggle, I was enrolled to contend, as at the beginning having the wrestling match against blood and flesh, but having surpassed the child and becoming a man, I am at the beginning against the rulers of the powers of this darkness, so that the struggle may be mine (Ps 38:6ab). This signifies that the Wrestler is the same as 'In the struggle, set my days' (Ps 38:6ab). Now it is possible for Substance to be said instead of Essence, such that the saying is this: my existence, being compared to yours, does not seem to be anything.

Another scripture contains: 'Behold, you have set my days of old, having a familiarity toward the old man whom I clothed' (Ps 38:6). Therefore also my substance, by which I existed in things prior to faith, is that nothing is before you except all things are vanity. All things on the earth—animals, plants, and the like—say all is vanity. Man alone living...

By these things, he is a participant in immortal life. As Psalm 38:7 says, he who, as he progresses, is being led through an image, makes this his work, being one conformed to the image of the Son of God.

But indeed every man lives being led through an image, either through that of God, observing what is according to the image, or through that of some other animal, becoming female or irrational according to its nature. And indeed the sensible and apparent world is an image of the intelligible and invisible. Man is not led through this world, which is an image, by his own will.

Having said these things concerning the common man, he says concerning each individual that they are in vain, being tossed about in the strivings concerning mortal things. For regarding each one, he says, 'He stores up and does not know for whom he gathers them' (Ps 38:8). For the one storing up upon the earth does not know who will inherit the wealth for which he himself labored; but the one storing up in heaven, having stored up for himself and not for another, knows the wealth that is inexpressible and unremovable from him.

If essence is said instead of substance, it is also from God as from a Creator; just as we exist, so this substance of ours is from Him, imparting to us the existence of things happening by necessity. Since, having hoped to be delivered from all my iniquities, I have not attained this (Ps 38:11), the fool reproaches, as if holding your handiwork in his hand: 'From the strength of the power of your hand I have been cut off' (Ps 38:12). For if the striking hand lashes strongly, the one being lashed is cut off by such a thing.

And from the present word we learn that the things being said are not other than the lashes of God, not rebuking [us]. For after saying, 'Remove your lashes from me,' they have come to be in reproofs concerning iniquity. For man is disciplined by reproofs offered concerning iniquity, his soul having been stretched out to cast away all fleshy thickness. Then indeed he is able to weave according to the spider, not having matter lying outside him, but bringing forth this from where and from himself. The word is able also to make manifest the unsubstantial nature of the evil thoughts of the soul, just as it is said in Isaiah concerning the sinners, 'They weave a spider's web' (Isa 59:5).

title: True Madness vs False Divination and the Fulfillment of Sacrifice
english: Let the spider-like webs of the reproaches against lawlessness be destroyed; the soul of the one reproached is spun like a spider's web (Ps 38:13-14).

Since he is not himself asking for much, he prays that he might be granted something to spend his life in, so that he might find refreshment after being worn out by perfect goods. For if he departs not as he should but as one lacking, he shall no longer exist—not in the sense of being destroyed into non-existence (for the soul is both immortal and indestructible), but in the sense of no longer being in participation of Being. For this is what truly is being: to participate in the One who says, 'I am the Being,' meaning that those not having this participation do not exist according to what was said in prayer to God: 'Do not give your scepter to those who are not' (Ps 39:3ab). Longing to participate in this existence, he prays that time might be given to him to find refreshment in the participation of Being, so that he may truly exist.

He calls idolatry a pit of misery, as those drawing from it are being miserable; for they draw nothing from that which is useful for life, just as Jeremiah, reproaching the Jews, said: 'They have dug for themselves broken pits, in which no water can be held' (Jer 2:13). Pleasures are a mud of clay, since they are dust and corruption of bodies and mere pits; whereas on the other hand, Christ saved the mortals through the faith in him and through the preaching.

Those who think that nothing is made manifest in the Scripture apart from the Word say: 'As one having attained a small good, he set the feet of the body upon the sensible rock, and thus he thanks the one who gifted this.' But we say that he who, having been freed from the aforementioned pit and mud, has been established upon the unshakeable and immovable perfection according to virtue, proclaims the things to come; for he follows the one standing on the rock, and his steps are directed by the passing Lord from evil to virtue and from mortal things to immortal things, and indeed according to every progress (Ps 39:4ab).

It is fitting that the moral discourse is new by the novelty of the spirit, and perhaps even new by Aisma, while theology is a hymn. He says that life's pursuits are to be called vanity, and false teachings and false prophecies are to be called madness. It should be noted, however, that as...
He added 'false' to 'madnesses' in contrast to true madnesses; for perhaps those seized prophetically possess a true madness, while false diviners possess a false madness.

Regarding Ps 39:6b, he speaks of the thoughts of God, meaning the deliberations occurring according to God's providence. To these, he says, no created thing shall be found resembling the mind of the Lord which knows all. Regarding Ps 39:6c, 'Your wonderful works and your thoughts'; for if anyone wished to examine something regarding depth, he would find it even more obscure than before: 'If I said, I will act wisely, but it has escaped from me far away, and a deep depth, who can find it?'

Regarding Ps 39:7, the Epistle to the Hebrews says that these upcoming verses are spoken from the face of the Savior concerning the Savior: 'Therefore, entering into the world, you said, a sacrifice and an offering you did not desire,' and the rest. This provided an occasion for him to speak the whole psalm, maintaining the same person until the end of what is said. Now, having passed the time of the shadow, according to which sacrifice and offering were brought, God, not wishing for worship through these things, perfected a body from the Virgin for the Son, so that whole burnt offerings and [sacrifices] concerning sin would no longer be pleasing. When the Savior said to the Father, 'Behold, I have come to do your will,' according to the will by which He [removes] the sin of the world, He himself, having been taken and brought forward for the sin of all, so that once remission has occurred, there is no longer a need for the sacrifice concerning sins.

Regarding Ps 39:8b-9a, he says the heading of the book calls all the God-breathed writing both legal and prophetic: 'For in this it is written concerning the coming conduct of the Savior.' And it is a heading because it summarizes all into one. And it is the becoming of the Savior a man, so that the will of the Lord might be done. It should be noted, however, that the concurrent will is something else, standing as a different will from the deliberative hypostasis which is of the one Willing.
Regarding Ps 39:9b, 'You have written it upon my leading principle.' And everyone who does according to the spiritual law has the law in his heart, that is, in his own disposition.
